messages.subject: Assistance needed on writing Deducer::descriptive.table
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

I am having some formatting/syntax issues writing the results of running a simple Analysis>Descriptives form a data set.

This is working

> FlightXY<- Deducer::descriptive.table(vars = d(X,Y) , strata = d(Date,Time),data= Flight_tracks, func.names =c("Mean"))
> write.table(FlightXY,'C:/CLN_Bat Project/T.txt',sep='\t')

However the written text file does not include the strata data and times.

The written file has this format:
Mean Mean.1 Mean.2 Mean.3 Mean.4
X 712237 716394.4 733617.3 706525
Y 3721762 3693663 3729273 3709741

If I run the Analysis>Descriptives pull down menu:

> descriptive.table(vars = d(X,Y) ,
+ strata = d(Date,Time),data= Flight_tracks,
+ func.names =c("Mean"))
The console shows this so it is stratified by dates and times.
$`Date: 02-07 Time: 00:00 `
     Mean
X  712237
Y 3721762

$`Date: 02-10 Time: 00:00 `
       Mean
X  716394.4
Y 3693663.5

$`Date: 02-13 Time: 00:00 `
       Mean
X  733617.3
Y 3729272.7

$`Date: 02-15 Time: 00:00 `
     Mean
X  706525
Y 3709741

How can I write the results to include the stratified grouping lables?

Tnx

Bruce

messages.subject: Can a function be added as a geom?
messages.subject_clean: Can a function be added as a geom?
messages.body_plain:
Hi. As I was looking at Ian's video on extending Plot Builder, I thought about adding a geom for Pareto Plots, which would remove an obstacle for some people looking at Deducer as a possibility.

The problem is that I don't know about the innards of geoms, so I thought that maybe I could build a function that returns a properly adjusted geom_bar and make it pass as a geom itself. The function is on the attached file, and it works fine for statements such as:

ggplot() + geom_myPareto(x=X,y=Y,data=DataPareto,colour = '#000000',fill = '#66ff33')

but of course it is not a true geom - and cannot get data.frame or aes, or any other parameters from ggplot().

The question is, can something like this be modified or wrapped so it can be added to Plot Builder as a geom? Or a template?

Suggestions would be much appreciated! Thanks,

Ben

messages.subject: Re: Can a function be added as a geom?
messages.subject_clean: Can a function be added as a geom?
messages.body_plain:
Ben,

A Pareto plot, with a “count” bar chart and a “percent total” line graph overlaid on the same plot, is not a single geom, but is a geom_bar() with a geom_line() (and probably a geom_point() overlaid on the geom_line()).

The last time I checked, ggplot2 didn't support multiple y axes on the same plot, so you can’t do such a graph in a single plot area. The closest you could come would be to arrange the two plots using grid.draw() {grid} or by using the viewport functions in {grid} to have the two plots arranged vertically (or side-by-side, if you prefer).

The basic code would look something like:

library(ggplot2)
library(grid)
p1 <- ggplot() + geom_bar()
p2 <- ggplot() + geom_line() + geom_point()
grid.draw(rbind(ggplotGrob(p1), ggplotGrob(p2), size = “first”)

You could also get a little fancier with {gtable}, per this Stack Overflow answer: http://stackoverflow.com/a/28256627/393354

I’m not familiar enough with Deducer’s plugin architecture to know if it could handle something like this.

Regards,

Tom

messages.body_plain:
James,

Did you also install the DeducerText library and load DeducerText after loading Deducer? Are you loading Deducer in JGR rather than the CRAN R GUI?

My normal workflow, after installing JGR, Deducer and DeducerText, would be

> library(JGR)
> JGR()

After JGR launches, I'd now be working in JGR:

> library(Deducer)
> library(DeducerText)

At this point, all the expected menus should show up in JGR.

If you could provide the steps needed reproduce the problem, we might be more successful at diagnosing the problem.

- Tom

—

messages.subject: Re: Text Menu in RConsole... DeducerText
messages.body_plain:
James,

It helps if you give details on the steps you performed to reproduce the problem, and include the results of SessionInfo().

Assuming you’re actually in JGR when you open the “Packages & Data” menu, select “Package Installer.” The dialog that pops up will either show a list of repositories, or a list of packages. If it’s repositories, select one near you. In the list of packages, scroll through until you find “DeducerText.” Select it. Click on “Install.” You only have to do this once; once it’s installed, you don’t have to install it the next time you run JGR.

With Deducer and DeducerText installed, type the command

library(“Deducer”)

Once Deducer loads, there will be a new submenu in “Packages & Data” called “GUI Add-Ons.” Select “Text.” This will load the DeducerText library.

You should now be good to go.

Note that the above will not work if you are in R.app (or R.exe, depending on which platform you’re using) as downloaded from CRAN. The CRAN R GUI cannot be used for Deducer.

- Tom

messages.body_plain:
Hi Tom & Ian,

Thanks a lot for your support.
I got clue from  http://www.r-statistics.com/2012/08/how-to-load-the-rjava-package-after-the-error-java_home-cannot-be-determined-from-the-registry/

Finally It worked for me.
The Problem is i think JRE Version. By default Java is provided 32 bit version for JRE But My system is 64 Bit.
I have manually downloaded 64 bit version of JRE from Java website . After that all works well... I followed below Tom's steps for Loading

My R version is 3.0.1  and now its working fine.

---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Did you also install the DeducerText library and load DeducerText after loading Deducer? Are you loading Deducer in JGR rather than the CRAN R GUI?

My normal workflow, after installing JGR, Deducer and DeducerText, would be

> library(JGR)
> JGR()

After JGR launches, I'd now be working in JGR:

> library(Deducer)
> library(DeducerText)

At this point, all the expected menus should show up in JGR.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Thanks Tom and Ian

Regards
